about.title: Laguna Woods Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Laguna Woods is home to a large retirement community, and falls on stairs, in clubhouses, parking structures, or along walkways near El Toro Road and Moulton Parkway are among the more common injury events reported here. Unlike a car crash, a fall on someone else's property raises a different legal question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard that caused you to fall? California law requires that showing before a premises liability claim can move forward. That's why documentation matters so much — photos of the spill, torn carpet, broken step, or poor lighting, along with any surveillance footage from the property, can make the difference in whether a claim succeeds. LawProactive doesn't practice law or negotiate on your behalf. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened and explain your options under California's two-year filing window.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Premises Liability Law

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify what evidence supports that timeline.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many properties overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can be critical to a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Bar, Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.question: I fell in a common area of my Laguna Woods community. Who's responsible?
items.answer: Responsibility often depends on who controls or maintains that specific area — it could be a homeowners association, a management company, or a private business, depending on where the fall happened. An attorney can help identify the right party and what maintenance or inspection records might apply.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit in California. If a government entity owns or maintains the property, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier administrative claim, so it's worth having your situation reviewed promptly.

items.question: What if I'm not sure the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: That's a common concern, and it's exactly the kind of question an attorney can help investigate. They may look at prior complaints, maintenance logs, or how long the hazard was present before your fall to determine whether notice can be established.
